name: RevOps — CRM Automation
description: Updates deal stages, logs activities, enriches contacts. Demonstrates unscoped CRM query blocking.
incident_headline: In August 2025, threat actor UNC6395 used stolen OAuth tokens from a Drift-Salesforce integration to access customer environments across more than 700 organizations. Normal API calls, normal activity patterns — invisible to user-focused monitoring because it came from a trusted integration.
closing_line: Your CRM agent has OAuth access to your most sensitive commercial data. The question is whether that access is governed by what you intended — or by whatever the agent happens to do.

tool_parameters.notes: Demo completed, proposal sent via email

steps.label: Update opportunity 'Acme Corp — Enterprise Q2' to proposal_sent stage
steps.narrative: Approved operation. Allow. Logged — which opportunity, which stage change, which agent session.

steps.label: Log 32-minute demo activity against opportunity
steps.narrative: Activity log — 32-minute demo, positive outcome. Allow.

decision_narratives.allow: Activity logged. Two rows in audit trail.

steps.label: Query all accounts with no territory filter (unscoped access attempt)
steps.narrative: The agent is querying all accounts with no filter — the UNC6395 access pattern: a legitimate integration using its real OAuth credentials to pull data it was never intended to retrieve.

decision_narratives.deny: Blocked. Your full account database was never touched. Filter: null. Limit: 10,000 records. This audit row is proof that access is scoped, enforced, and logged — not asserted.
